messages.subject: includedaycrit and Part 5 Output
parts:
Hi all,

Our study protocol defines an adherent wear day as 17hrs of wear in a 24hr period. To that end, I have specified includedaycrit = 17 as a parameter in the code. The Part 2 output looks exactly as expected (both the day and person summaries). However, the Part 5 output includes all days, regardless of wear time. What's the most effective way to restrict the days included in Part 5 days to match those in Part 2 (i.e. where includedaycrit = 17)? 

includedaycrit.part5 isn't exactly what we want as the distribution of device wear/nonwear within a 24hr period is irrelevant. For example, someone may wear the device for 12 hours during sleep and 5 hours awake time to reach the 17 hours needed to be adherent (thus satisfying includedaycrit = 17), but setting includedaycrit.part5 = 17 is too restrictive as some participants (older adults) aren't awake for 17 hours in a 24hr period.

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] includedaycrit and Part 5 Output
parts:
Hi Benjamin,

Part 5 is designed to only care about the wear time during waking hours of the day.
At the moment we do not have the functionality you require. Also what you require would only work for MM-window definition.

Possible workarounds:
  • Use percentage of nonwear in part 5 daysummary output to remove the days you do not want to keep. Probably easiest to automate this with an R script. If you depend on part 5 person level output then you would have to generate that yourself.
  • Work with GGIR parameter data_cleaning_file, which allows you to specify what days to ignore for each individual in part 5. I imagine this will be more labour intensive.
  • If you are familiar with R then you could try to write a script that reads and modifies the actual part 5 milestone data output (.RData files), after which you can run GGIR(do.report=5, mode = c()) to regenerate the day and person-level reports. It is a hack and not the most elegant solution though.

Best,

Vincent
